clue.text: Conservative girl in charge of one of five races

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Tory lass is put in charge of running a big race.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain has five flat horse races called the Classics, among them the Derby and the St Leger.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the five major British flat races for three-year-old horses is known as a Classic.

clue.text: Caught variety show journalist attended at farm building

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: variety suggests a mix, so the letters of show are rearranged

parts.note: ED, an editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter at a variety show staged on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' turns SHOW into OWSH, which follows C and precedes ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is a barn where cattle are housed on a farm.

clue.text: One on the look out for sign of a famous person

definitions.text: One on the look out for sign of a famous person

parts.words: One on the look out for sign of a famous person
parts.note: sign reads as signature: someone hoping for a celebrity's signed name, not a glimpse of them

explanation.surface: A fan watching for any trace of a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectors of celebrity signatures hunt them down eagerly.

clue.text: Hard worker pulls up

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tows means pulls

explanation.surface: A diligent labourer heaves things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is a student who studies very hard.

clue.text: Ignore the girl-it could be injurious

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Snubbing a girl could hurt her feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, a weapon that can wound.

clue.text: Bill has heart trouble gripping another part of the body

indicators.note: gripping says one piece holds the other inside it
trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of heart are stirred into a new order

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A patient with a heart problem finds a second organ affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns HEART into TRHEA, and 'gripping' puts AC inside it after TR.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is an organ of the body, and 'another' follows on from the heart in the surface.

clue.text: Willing to go

parts.note: read as having made a will before going, that is dying, rather than being keen to leave

explanation.surface: Someone happy to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying having made a legal will is the legal state described.

clue.text: Distinctive character of topless girl

indicators.note: topless in a down clue says the first letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Laura is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A topless girl has a certain air about her.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality around someone.

clue.text: An accommodating person

parts.note: accommodating read literally as providing lodging, not as being obliging

explanation.surface: Someone helpful and obliging.
explanation.definitionFit: The owner of an inn provides rooms for guests.

clue.text: Strange that war went from one side to the other

definitions.text: from one side to the other

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd war that moved across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across, crosswise from side to side.

clue.text: Nobody withdrawing completely unharmed

definitions.meaning: in racing a horse taken out of a race is a scratch, so a field with no withdrawals is one without any
escaping with not even a graze

explanation.surface: A race in which no runner pulled out and nobody was hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratching is a racing withdrawal, and emerging with no scratch also means suffering no injury at all.

clue.text: Intoxicated above the normal level

definitions.meaning: drunk or drugged, in an elevated state

explanation.surface: Someone drunk, rising above the usual line.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stoned is called being elevated, and anything raised beyond the usual mark is also described that way.

clue.text: Artilleryman leaving vehicle in Ulster town

indicators.note: leaving says the gunner goes out of the vehicle, so his letters are taken away

parts.note: a caravan is a vehicle towed behind a car
RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner

explanation.surface: A gunner climbs out of his van in a town in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster's nine counties include Cavan, now in the Irish Republic; Cavan is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavan is a county town in the historic province of Ulster.

clue.text: Lamb, one following an old priest

indicators.note: following places the single letter after the priest

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
A means one

explanation.surface: A lamb trotting after a priest of old.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb, the English essayist, wrote under the pen name Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist Charles Lamb signed his Essays with this pseudonym.

clue.text: Some tender massaged skin

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sore skin being given a gentle massage.
explanation.definitionFit: The dermis is the layer of the body's outer covering.

clue.text: Choir repulsed by discharge from an ulcer

indicators.note: repulsed suggests being driven back in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Singers recoiling from a festering wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichor is a watery fluid oozing from a sore or wound.

clue.text: Artists' furniture

definitions.meaning: people who draw pictures, read here as a plural noun
sliding boxes in a chest or desk

explanation.surface: The tables and chairs found in a painter's studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Artists'' is surface dressing: the first definition is simply those who draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmen who sketch are those who draw, and a chest of storage compartments is also called this.

clue.text: Leave out, right in the passage

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for right inside the verb

parts.note: to except is to leave out or exclude

explanation.surface: An editor cutting a section and keeping only the correct part.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract quoted from a book or text is a passage taken out of it.

clue.text: Has performed with me in the commercial although was embarrassed

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the advert

parts.note: AD, an advertisement, is a commercial

indicators.note: performed suggests the letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor who appeared in a TV advert is now mortified by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' turns HAS into SHA; with ME that gives SHAME, which goes 'in' AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling shame or awkwardness is being embarrassed, a near synonym.

clue.text: Tumbler or revolutionary graduate in the act

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the act

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so or is read backwards

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A glass or a radical graduate appears in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns OR into RO; RO plus BA go 'in' ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a gymnast who performs flips and somersaults.

clue.text: Divert from European land

parts.note: de is the French, a European language, for from
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Turning away from a stretch of continental territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract attention is to divert or draw it away.

clue.text: Do well as a Shakespearean leaving nothing behind

indicators.note: leaving says the zero letter at the back goes away

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest
O is nothing, and behind places it at the tail end

explanation.surface: An actor in a Shakespeare play is told to succeed without leaving anything behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive or flourish is to do well.

clue.text: Approval of check after record upset

indicators.note: after puts the check following the record
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the record is read backwards

parts.note: LP, a long-playing record
an audit is a check of accounts

explanation.surface: Approval of an inspection after an album flopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or approval.

clue.text: Rum sort vandalised the platform

indicators.note: vandalised means damaged and wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd sort of person wrecked the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stage for a speaker.

clue.text: Utter defeat going almost all the way

indicators.note: almost all says the last letter of the road is dropped

parts.note: a route is a way

explanation.surface: A team beaten completely, having gone nearly the full distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A crushing defeat in which the losers are put to flight.

clue.text: Hurries back with a short instrument

indicators.note: back says the word for hurries is read from end to start

parts.note: darts means hurries or dashes

explanation.surface: A musician rushing home with a little instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' marks an abbreviation: Strad is short for Stradivarius, a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius violin is often known by its clipped name.

clue.text: The man's second disapproving noise

parts.note: his means belonging to the man

explanation.surface: A man's second remark draws a jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences show disapproval by making a sibilant sound like a snake.

clue.text: To cover with wax gives some nice results

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Waxing a surface gives pleasing results.
explanation.definitionFit: To cere is to wrap or coat in waxed cloth, as with a shroud.

clue.text: Article in study of church dignitary

indicators.note: in places the article inside the room

parts.note: a den is a private study
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay found in a cleric's study.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is the senior clergyman of a cathedral.

clue.text: Is this how gamblers continue to improve?

definitions.text: Is this how gamblers continue to improve?

parts.words: Is this how gamblers continue to improve?
parts.note: one gambler after another, those who bet, sound like a phrase meaning improving steadily

explanation.surface: Asking whether punters keep on getting better at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means improving ever more, and a gambler is one who bets, giving a pun.

clue.text: Alternatively plunge into the river, it's a rushing stream

indicators.note: plunge into puts the word for alternatively inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
or means alternatively

explanation.surface: Either dive into the river or not, since it is flowing fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast violent flow of water.

clue.text: Fit to have a drink after so much French

indicators.note: after puts the drink following the French word

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit to drink

explanation.surface: Ready to have a drink after so much French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a fit of temper.
